description:
FILED s400.  The work is DONE and measured; what is missing is the two
blockers below and a decision to accept the remaining cost.

WHY.  test.pl's which_perl() names the interpreter a test spawns a child with.
Until s400 PCL's version returned a hard-coded real-perl path, so those
children ran PERL: every assertion about the child compared perl to perl and
said nothing about PCL.  That is exactly the vacuous-child problem #90 removed
for fresh_perl_*/runperl by pointing them at tools/pclperl-for-tests via
$PCLPERL, and perl-tests/t/test.pl's _pcl_child_perl is the resolution to
mirror (PCLPERL, else $^X; PCL_FRESH_PERL=real forces real perl).

s400 landed only the machine-portability half (which_perl returns $^X, derived
at runtime -- see cl/pcl-test.lisp, task #207/#278).  The $PCLPERL half was
implemented and measured, then held: USER call, "hygiene only".

THE MEASUREMENT (all 19 companion callers + the full sweep, s400):
  * SEVENTEEN of the 19 companion files are UNMOVED.
  * op/closure.t   267/3 -> 235/27.  Its closure matrix runs under PCL for the
    first time.  The 24 new not-oks are one family: a NAMED sub inside an ANON
    sub closing over the enclosing foreach/filescope variable -- PCL's own
    compiler announces it ("Parser2 TODO: lexical 'foreach' possibly captured
    by nested sub named_57").  Task #347.
  * perl-tests/closure.t (the sweep's copy)  OK 272/0 -> PARTIAL 240/28, and
    64 s instead of a few.  PARTIAL means it stops early (child exit 65280),
    so ten rows never run at all.
  * run/cloexec.t  16/6 -> HANG at its first backtick child, still hanging at
    --timeout 400.  Task #346.

WHY IT WAS HELD.  #176/#204: a file that aborts or times out contributes NO
rows, and coverage evaporating invisibly is the failure mode this project
guards hardest against.  Trading two measurement HOLES for ~56 vacuous rows
made honest is the wrong direction while those rules stand -- but only until
#346 and #347 are fixed, which is why this task is blocked by them, not
closed.

TO LAND IT (the diff is four lines): in cl/pcl-test.lisp, pl-which_perl
resolves $PCLPERL first unless PCL_FRESH_PERL=real, exactly as
_pcl_child_perl does, falling back to $^X.  Then re-run the 19 companion
callers and the sweep, splice the moved rows with their causes, and edit the
sweep baselines ROW BY ROW (never re-bless) for whatever closure.t still
loses.


RULED s401 (docs/fable-answers-s400.md Â§7.2): the release condition IS
"#346 and #347 fixed", in that order â #346 first (a harness bug in
tools/pclperl-for-tests, own filler), then #347 (own half-session,
Pl/t/closure-01.t extended first), then this switch lands with row-by-row
baseline edits.  Land-early-and-register REJECTED: a deliberate HANG in the
companion run is the tail #345 removes, and closure.t PARTIAL loses ten
sweep rows.  Sessions C and G of docs/plan-post-s400.md.


LANDED s406 (5376d99).  With #347 and #358 fixed the switch costs NOTHING: the 19 companion callers are byte-identical in their failure logs before and after, the full sweep is GATE clean at TOTAL 18517 (closure.t stays OK 272/4, pack.t OK 5636/89), gate 146/5346.  Proof the children really switched: op/closure.t + run/cloexec.t take 28 s with PCL children vs 7.7 s under PCL_FRESH_PERL=real.  ONE companion row moved — io/crlf_through.t 726/216 DIFF -> 942/0 OK — and NOT as a fix: that file pipes through a which_perl child, so both ends now share PCL's :crlf gap (task #139).  Recorded in docs/perl-suite-run.tsv.
subject: which_perl's children should run PCL ($PCLPERL) like fresh_perl/runperl do (#90) - IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED s400, held by two measurement holes (USER call)
